info.name: Tasks API
info.description:
Spring Boot `tasks` API (http://localhost:8080).

## First run
1. **0. Setup**: creates the `userEmail` and `adminEmail` accounts (both get the USER role).
2. Grant ADMIN to the second account (no admin is created automatically):
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES ('<adminId>', 'ADMIN');
   ```
   `adminId` is stored in the collection variables after sign-up.
3. **Auth**: run "Login — user" and "Login — admin". Access tokens expire after 15 minutes: run "Refresh — user" to get a new one without logging in again.
4. **Email verification**: needs the Mailpit service of `compose.yaml` (web UI on http://localhost:8025).
5. Then run *Tasks*, *Task events* and *Cleanup* in order (or use the Collection Runner).

## Authentication
Bearer JWT. Each request uses `{{userToken}}` or `{{adminToken}}` depending on the role it needs. Requests suffixed with (401), (403) or (404) check error cases.

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Run in order on first start. See the collection description to promote the admin account.

request.description: Public. Creates an account with the USER role. Running it again with the same email returns 409 (email already taken).
Public. Creates the future admin (USER role). Then grant ADMIN in SQL and log in again.
Public. Stores the JWT in `userToken` and `accessToken`, and the user ID (`uid` claim) in `userId`. Also stores the refresh token in `userRefreshToken`.
Public. Stores the JWT in `adminToken`. The test fails if the account does not have the ADMIN role yet. Also stores the refresh token in `adminRefreshToken`.
Public. Exchanges the refresh token for a new access token and a rotated refresh token. Stores both, and keeps the used one in `previousUserRefreshToken`.
Replaying a rotated token is treated as theft: returns 401 and revokes the whole token family, including the latest `userRefreshToken`. Log in again afterwards.
Starts a new token family, since the previous one was revoked by the reuse detection above.

item.name: Email verification
item.description: Sign-up sends a verification email to Mailpit. These requests read it through the Mailpit API, so no copy-paste is needed. Login does not require a verified email.

request.description: Authenticated. Sends a new link and invalidates the previous one.
Reads the local Mailpit inbox (compose.yaml, web UI on http://localhost:8025). Results are sorted newest first.

exec: // Emails are sent asynchronously after commit: give the SMTP catcher a moment

Public. Marks the email as verified; the token is single-use and expires after 24 hours.

item.name: Notification settings
item.description: Email notification preferences, one switch per task event. Everything is enabled until the user changes it.

request.description: ADMIN or the user themselves. A user who never changed anything gets the defaults.

exec: pm.test('all enabled by default', () => pm.expect([body.taskAssigned, body.taskUnassigned, body.taskCancelled, body.taskDeleted]).to.eql([true, true, true, true]));

item.name: Password reset
item.description: Forgot-password flow. The reset email is read from Mailpit. Confirming signs the user out everywhere (refresh tokens revoked) and marks the email as verified.
